title: spec pins: gate 4 reads a pinned scope, not the branch
acceptance: Implements design.md section 15.5 exactly. On a task's first round fm-worker.sh writes state/pins/<project>/<task>/1.json (project, task, engine commit, task-list path, verbatim spec, its SHA-256, design path, target base commit, and T-043's contract for the project verbatim — the whole block, `docs` included — with the engine main commit it was read from and its SHA-256) and emits spec_pinned. The contract always comes from the engine main head at pin time, including for a self-hosted task whose spec is pinned from its own branch. The engine commit is the engine main head containing the task; for the self project a task not on main is pinned from its own branch's commit, else from the engine working copy with engine_commit null.

fm-worker.sh, fm-review.sh and fm-gate.sh read the task spec from the highest-numbered pin through one library function in bin/fm-config.sh, never from the target branch or the engine working copy. With an engine commit the spec is re-derived and its hash compared; without one the branch's own entry must match the pin's hash. The contract is re-derived from its recorded commit and hash-checked in both cases; repin reads spec and contract afresh from the new commit.

Gate 4 fails with no pin, a hash mismatch, a changed file outside the pinned scope, a self-hosted branch whose own task entry differs from its pin, and any `.fm-*` path. Each failure names its reason.

`fm-project.sh repin --task <t> --decision D-<n>` writes the next pin and emits spec_repinned only when the decision is a decision_made for that project and task with its authorizing option and the new engine commit is on main with a differing spec; otherwise it refuses with a message and writes nothing. Pin files are append-only.
Self-hosting keeps working after this task alone: with no --project, and with the firstmate-workflow project named explicitly, every existing caller, fixture and test behaves as before.
Evidence is this pull request's required GitHub check and the seven gates. New behaviour gets tests written to fail first; the worker does not run the suite itself.
Stay inside this scope. If the work needs a file outside it, stop and name the file and the reason.
